src: I.A.S. (Pre) 1993
s: A fertile soil, suitable for growing common crops is likely to have a pH value of :
x: The soil pH is a measure of the acidity or alkalinity in soils. A pH below 7 is acidic and above 7 is alkaline. Soil pH is considered a master variable in soils as it controls many chemical processes that take place. It specifically affects plant nutrient availability by controlling the chemical forms of the nutrients. Most nutrients that plants need can dissolve easily when the pH of the soil solution ranges from 6.0 to 7.0. Thus, option (c) is correct.

src: Uttarakhand P.C.S. (Pre) 2025
s: According to the Koppen's Climate Classification the (Amw) climate is found predominantly in which part of India?
x: According to Koppen's Climate Classification, the 'Amw' climate (tropical monsoon type with a short dry winter season) is found mainly in western coastal region of India. ii. Rainfall *Generally in India rainfall occurs from the month of June to September when south-west monsoon is effective throughout the country. In this period, the low-pressure zone of North- Western India is very intense and systematic. Due to low air pressure, south-east winds from the tropic of Capricorn in the Southern Hemisphere cross the equator and are attracted towards the Indian Peninsula. Passing over the oceans these winds are filled with humidity and split into two branches - Arabian Sea branch and Bay of Bengal branch. *When the south-west monsoon winds enter the terrestrial area, it rains with an intense thundering and torrential storms. The arrival of these winds and rainfall is called ‘burst’ of the monsoon. *The speed of these winds is about 30 km/h on average and they become effective throughout the country within a month. *According to the data Rainfall Statistics of India (2024), almost the entire rainfall is received from the southwest monsoon (June-September). *Monsoon winds of the Arabian Sea are obstructed by the Western Ghats. These winds climb the slope of the Western Ghats and soon become cool causing heavy rainfall on the windward side of Western Ghats. These winds cause little rainfall to the east of the Western Ghats. The region of low rainfall is known as the rain-shadow area
